## Teaching points

1. A prior withdrawal seizure increases the risk of a complicated course. Treat withdrawal and monitor mental status, breathing and vital signs.
2. Prior complicated withdrawal supports monitored inpatient management. Reassess symptoms, consciousness and breathing after each sedating dose.
3. Thiamine and nutritional/electrolyte assessment accompany withdrawal treatment; medication response is not a reason to discharge a high-risk patient alone.
